editions.note: Sixth edition, catch-up after the 21–22 usage outage: Excel Insert Chart, a Word Navigation pane, and PowerPoint Slide Sorter. Jared's 👍 on #588, #589 and #590 is applied (approved). #548 is partly shipped in v0.2.0 (el.dirty + nitro-change; React onDirtyChange still in draft PR #597). #546 is building in draft PR #605.

Fifth edition: Excel borders, fill colour and Merge & Center; Format Painter and Clear Formatting in all three apps; and a host API to hide, add and run ribbon commands. #577 and #579 are approved; #578 (comments) was declined.
Fourth edition: Excel Sort & Filter, Word comments (with a host hook), and Word headers, footers and page numbers.
Third edition: right-click menus, Insert link (Ctrl+K), and Print / Save as PDF. #546, #547 and #548 are approved; #540 is in draft PR #555; #542 is building.
Second edition: Word word count, Excel Freeze Panes, and an unsaved-changes API for host apps. #540 and #542 are building in tonight's nightly; #541 is queued.
First edition: three proposals after the v0.1.0 npm release.

proposals.headline: Turn a selected range into a chart, from a new Insert tab
proposals.today_caption: Today: Excel has only File, Home and View. There is no Insert tab and no way to make a chart, so a selected range of numbers (A1:D6 here) stays a range of numbers.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: a new Insert tab with Insert Chart. The gallery offers Column, Bar, Line and Pie; a clustered column chart of A1:D6 lands on the sheet as a movable object.
proposals.why: You can already open a workbook that contains a chart — the painter shipped in M1 — but you cannot make one. Excel, Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and Collabora all put Insert Chart next to the selection. Nitro has no Insert tab on Excel today, so a range of numbers stays a range of numbers.
proposals.effort_note: 3–4 days (Insert tab with a Charts group, gallery of clustered column/bar/line/pie, write a standard chart part and two-cell anchor from one contiguous range, reuse the existing chart painter, move/resize, one undo, save round-trip)
proposals.risk: Medium. Chart XML (chart part, colours, cached values, drawing anchor) must reopen in Excel and LibreOffice without repair, and the cache must match the range so Excel does not prompt to update. Out of scope: combo charts, secondary axes, pivot charts and chart sheets.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the Insert tab and gallery load with a lazily loaded Excel ribbon chunk (a few KB). Painting reuses the existing chart painter. The loader stays under 17,408 B.
dod: Excel gains an Insert tab (File, Home, Insert, View) with a Charts group; Insert Chart opens a gallery of Column, Bar, Line and Pie.
With a contiguous range of numbers selected, choosing a type inserts a chart object on the sheet, titled from the range, with a legend; the range remains the source.
The chart is one undo step, can be moved and resized, and is saved as standard chart and drawing parts; files reopen in Excel and LibreOffice without repair and still paint in Nitro.
Editing a source cell updates the chart after the edit is committed.
Playwright tests cover each type, undo, move, save round-trip and OOXML/LibreOffice validation; Font, Alignment and Number groups stay at two rows; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Jump to any heading from a Navigation pane
proposals.today_caption: Today: View has only Zoom and Diagnostics. Headings are in the page, but there is no list of them, so you scroll to find a section. Ctrl+F opens a find box that does not even focus the search field.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: View > Navigation (or Ctrl+F) opens a left pane with Headings, Pages and Results. The heading on screen is highlighted; click one to jump to it.
proposals.why: Word, Google Docs (the document outline) and OnlyOffice all offer a headings list so you can jump around a long document without scrolling. Nitro already paginates and knows paragraph styles (Title, Heading 1–3), and v0.2.0 added get/setPosition, so a jump is a scroll, not a new layout engine. Ctrl+F today opens a find box that does not focus the search field; this puts Find in a Navigation pane with Headings, Pages and Results, the way Word does.
proposals.effort_note: 1–2 days (Navigation button on View, heading walk from styles, click-to-scroll, Pages list, Results reuses today's find and focuses the box, Ctrl+F)
proposals.risk: Low. The pane is read-mostly and does not change the file. Headings without a heading style are omitted, as in Word's outline. Navigation is one button in the existing Show group on View, so Font and Paragraph stay at two rows.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: a few KB in the lazily loaded Word chrome chunk. The heading list is built from the already-loaded document model; jump uses the existing scroll and position APIs. The loader stays under 17,408 B.
dod: View > Navigation (pressed while open) shows a left pane with Headings, Pages and Results; Ctrl+F opens it on Results with the search box focused.
Headings lists Title and Heading 1–3 in document order, indents by level, and highlights the heading currently on screen; click or Enter scrolls that heading into view and moves the caret.
The list updates after typing, style changes and undo; an empty document or a document with no headings shows a short empty state.
Pages lists one row per page and jumps to that page. Results is today's find (replace stays with #542) inside the same pane.
Playwright tests cover open/close, click-to-jump, keyboard, empty state and focused search; Font and Paragraph stay at two rows; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: See every slide at once and drag to reorder, in Slide Sorter view
proposals.today_caption: Today: View has Zoom, a Slide pane toggle and Previous/Next. The only way to see the deck is the narrow left rail in Normal view, so checking the flow or reordering several slides means a lot of scrolling and Move Slide Up/Down.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: View > Slide Sorter fills the canvas with a grid of every slide, with number and title. The current slide is outlined; drag a slide to reorder, double-click to return to Normal.
proposals.why: PowerPoint's Slide Sorter is how people check the flow of a deck and reorder several slides at a glance. Nitro already paints thumbnails for the left rail and already has Move Slide Up/Down, but View has no sorter, so you only ever see one big slide plus a narrow strip. This is a layout of those thumbs, plus drag-to-reorder. It is not a slide show (that remains deferred).
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (View > Slide Sorter and Normal, a wrapping thumbnail grid, click to select, drag to reorder, Delete and Ctrl+D, double-click or Escape to return, save keeps the new order)
proposals.risk: Low. Reorder is the same operation as today's Move Slide Up/Down, as one undo step. Hidden slides, if any, stay hidden but remain in the grid, as PowerPoint does. This must not invent a slide-show or presenter view.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: a few KB in the lazily loaded PowerPoint chrome chunk. Thumbnails already rendered for the rail are reused. The loader stays under 17,408 B.
dod: View > Slide Sorter (and a Normal button) switches the canvas to a grid of all slides at a readable size, with slide number and title; the current slide is outlined.
Drag-and-drop reorders slides; Delete removes the selected slide; Ctrl+D duplicates it; each change is one undo step and survives save.
Click selects; double-click, View > Normal or Escape returns to Normal on that slide; arrow keys and Previous/Next move the selection.
Playwright tests cover open, reorder, delete, duplicate, undo, return to Normal and save; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Colour cells, add borders and Merge & Center from Excel's Home tab
proposals.today_caption: Today: Excel Home > Font has Bold, Italic, Underline, Strikethrough and font size only. There is no Borders, Fill Color or Font Color, and Alignment has no Merge & Center, so you can't format a simple table.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Borders, Fill Color and Font Color split buttons join the two-row Font group, and Merge & Center joins Alignment. The Borders menu is open; B12:F15 shows a merged, filled title row and All Borders.
proposals.why: Borders, fill colour, font colour and Merge & Center are the most-used buttons on Excel's Home tab, and Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and Collabora all put them in the same place. Nitro already paints fills, borders and merged cells that arrive in a file, the style writer already pools fills and borders, and the command ids (home.borders, home.fill-color, home.font-color, home.merge-center) are registered. But none of them are on the ribbon or wired to an edit, so you can't turn a range of numbers into a readable table.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (ribbon split buttons and palettes, three style edits plus merge/unmerge on the existing writer, undo, save round-trip)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. New fills and borders must dedupe into styles.xml (no style explosion on repeated clicks), and mergeCells must stay valid: merging over data keeps only the top-left value, with Excel's warning. Font group stays at two rows: the three new split buttons replace no existing control.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: palettes and the Borders menu load with the lazily loaded Excel ribbon chunk (a few KB). Each click is one style edit on the selection; painting fills and borders already exists.
dod: Home > Font gains Borders, Fill Color and Font Color split buttons (last-used colour on the face, palette with theme and standard colours plus No Fill / Automatic); the Font group stays at two rows.
Borders menu offers Bottom, Top, Left, Right, No Border, All Borders, Outside Borders and Thick Box Border; each applies to the selection as one undo step.
Home > Alignment gains Merge & Center with Merge Across, Merge Cells and Unmerge Cells; merging over data keeps the top-left value and warns first, as Excel does.
Saved files reopen in Excel and LibreOffice without repair, with fills, borders, font colours and merges intact; repeated formatting reuses existing styles.xml entries (validator + round-trip in CI).
Playwright tests cover each border type, fill, font colour, merge/unmerge, undo and a save round-trip; bundle-budget and all required checks green; no first-load size limit raised.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-20 (👍). Queued behind the host-API priority work. Label applied on the 2026-11-22 catch-up run.

proposals.headline: Format Painter and Clear Formatting: copy a look in one click, or wipe it
proposals.today_caption: Today: Home > Clipboard has Cut, Copy and Paste only. There is no Format Painter, and Home > Font has no Clear All Formatting button, so matching or resetting a look means redoing each setting by hand.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Format Painter in Clipboard (pressed) and Clear All Formatting in Font row 1. The look of “What we shipped” is copied, then painted onto a bullet line with the brush cursor.
proposals.why: Format Painter is one of the most-used buttons in all three Office apps, and Google Docs, Sheets and Slides (paint format), OnlyOffice and Collabora (Clone Formatting) all have it. Today, making one heading, cell or text box look like another means repeating font, size, colour and alignment by hand, and there is no one-click way back to plain text. The command ids (home.format-painter, home.clear-formats) are already registered; this wires them to the selection with one shared implementation across Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (capture/apply of run + paragraph properties in Word and PowerPoint, cell style in Excel; brush cursor and sticky mode; Clear Formatting)
proposals.risk: Low. Painting is a normal formatting edit of the target, so it reuses existing run, paragraph and cell-style writers and is one undo step. Edge cases: painting a paragraph mark copies paragraph formatting (as Word does); Excel paints over a range by size; Esc must cancel sticky mode and leave focus in the document.
proposals.perf: No first-load change and a few KB in each lazy ribbon chunk. Capture is a read of the current selection; apply is one edit.
dod: Home > Clipboard gains Format Painter in all three apps; single click paints once, double click stays on until Esc or a second click; Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V copy and paste formatting.

Word and PowerPoint: copies character formatting (font, size, bold/italic/underline, colour, highlight) and, when the source includes the paragraph mark, paragraph formatting; Excel copies the full cell style (number format, font, fill, borders, alignment) to the painted range.
Home > Font gains Clear All Formatting (Word/PowerPoint: back to the paragraph style's defaults; Excel: Clear Formats) without adding a ribbon row.
Each paint or clear is one undo step and survives save; files reopen in Office and LibreOffice without repair.
Playwright tests cover paint once, sticky paint, Esc, clear, undo and save round-trip in each app; bundle-budget and all required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-20 (👍). Queued behind the host-API priority work. Label applied on the 2026-11-22 catch-up run.

proposals.headline: Let host apps hide, add and run ribbon commands (ribbon option, execCommand, nitro-command event)
proposals.today_caption: Today: an embedding app gets the full or embedded toolbar as-is. It can't hide Open or Insert Picture, can't add its own “Send for review” button, and has no public way to run a command like Bold from its own UI.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the host hid Open and added “Insert clause” and “Send for review” to the embedded toolbar. Clicking a host button fires nitro-command; the code card shows the ribbon option and execCommand.
proposals.why: Every host that embeds an editor wants to trim commands it doesn't support (Open, Save As, Insert Picture) and add one or two of its own (Send for review, Insert clause, Submit). OnlyOffice and Collabora both expose this through their integration APIs. Nitro already has a single command registry shared by the ribbon and shortcuts (ids like home.bold, file.open, insert.picture), so exposing it as a small, typed host API is cheap. It also fixes the stringly typed applyEdit gap in #531 for the common case.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (ribbon option on the element and React prop, hide/add in both toolbar modes, execCommand + typed id union, nitro-command event, docs)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. Command ids become public API, so they need a stable, documented list (generated from the registry) and a guard test. Host buttons must respect readonly and keyboard focus order, and must never inject HTML: label and icon are text and SVG path data only, which keeps the strict-CSP goal in #573.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the option is read when the ribbon is first built, and hidden commands are simply not rendered. execCommand dispatches through the existing registry. No new chunk.
dod: el.ribbon = { hide: [...ids], add: [{ id, label, icon?, tab?, group?, primary?, menu? }] } (and a React ribbon prop) works in full and embedded modes. Hidden ids vanish from ribbon, menus and shortcuts; added buttons appear in the named tab/group, or at the end of the embedded toolbar.

el.execCommand(id, args?) runs any registered command with a typed id union in index.d.ts and returns false (with the valid ids in the error) for unknown ids; el.commands lists ids with label, shortcut and enabled state.
A nitro-command event (cancelable) fires for every command, host-added or built in, with { id, format }. preventDefault() lets a host replace built-ins such as file.save or file.open.
Readonly disables editing commands, including host ones flagged editing: true; tests cover hide, add, execCommand, cancel and readonly in all three apps.
README host-API section documents the option, the generated command-id list and an example; bundle-budget and all required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-20 (👍). Queued behind the host-API priority work. Label applied on the 2026-11-22 catch-up run.

proposals.headline: Sort and Filter a spreadsheet, with AutoFilter arrows on the header row
proposals.today_caption: Today: there is no Data tab and no Sort or Filter command; the first row has no AutoFilter arrows, so you can't hide or sort rows from the UI.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Data > Sort & Filter (Sort A to Z, Sort Z to A, Filter). AutoFilter arrows sit on the first row; the open menu searches, sorts and checks values, as in Excel.
proposals.why: Sorting a column and filtering a table are among the first things people do in a real spreadsheet, and Excel, Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and Collabora all put AutoFilter arrows on the header row. Nitro already keeps an autoFilter that arrives in a file and has SUBTOTAL / filtered-row helpers in the formula engine, but you can't turn Filter on, pick values, or Sort A to Z from the UI, and there is no Data tab. Wiring that up makes Nitro usable for everyday list work, and gives the already-approved right-click menu real Sort and Filter commands to call.
proposals.effort_note: 3–4 days (toggle AutoFilter, value menu, sort of the current region, and a valid autoFilter part on save)
proposals.risk: Medium. The saved autoFilter must open in Excel without a repair prompt, and hidden rows must stay out of copy, fill and later sort. Sort rearranges values in the current region (header row stays put) and is one undo step; formulas that pointed at moved cells follow Excel's usual relative-reference behaviour. A table without a clear header row should still get arrows on the first row of the used range, as Excel does.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the Data tab and filter menu load with the lazily loaded Excel ribbon chunk (a few KB). Filtering hides rows already in the sheet view; it does not rescan the workbook on open. Sort is a single edit of the current region.
dod: A Data tab (and Home > Editing if it fits in the existing group without adding a ribbon row) offers Sort A to Z, Sort Z to A and Filter; Ctrl+Shift+L toggles AutoFilter on the current region.

With Filter on, the first row of the region shows AutoFilter arrows; the menu has Search, Sort A to Z / Z to A, Select All, per-value checkboxes and Blanks; OK hides non-matching rows and is one undo step.

Sort A to Z / Z to A rearranges the data rows of the current region and leaves the header row in place; the result saves as a valid autoFilter / sorted sheet that Excel and LibreOffice reopen without repair.
Hidden rows stay hidden while the filter is on, and are skipped by copy of the visible region; clearing the filter or turning Filter off shows them again.

Playwright tests cover toggle, one value filter, sort, undo and a save round-trip; bundle-budget and all required checks green. No first-load size limit is raised; new code stays in the lazy Excel chunk.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-20 (👍). Queued behind the host-API priority work.

proposals.headline: Add comments in the margin, and let host apps hook into them
proposals.today_caption: Today: there is no Review tab and no comment balloons. You can't attach a comment to a phrase, and a host app has no comment API to call.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Review > Comments (New Comment, Delete, Resolve, Previous, Next). A highlighted phrase opens a margin card to reply or resolve, as in Word and Google Docs.
proposals.why: Comments are how people review a document in Word, Google Docs, OnlyOffice and Collabora, and they are one of the main reasons a host app wants getSelection() — to anchor a note to a phrase. Nitro already has the model and edit ops to add, reply, resolve and delete Word comments, but there is no Review tab, no margin balloon, and no host event. Shipping the UI (and a small host hook) lets reviewers work in the document and lets embedding apps show or create the same comments.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (Review tab and margin cards on top of the existing add/reply/resolve/delete ops; finish comments.xml identity on save if needed)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. Saved comments must be valid word/comments.xml (and the document relationships) so Word opens the file without a repair prompt. Anchors must follow the selected text when the paragraph is edited, and resolved comments stay in the file but render in a quiet state, as Word does. No live multiplayer is in scope.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the Review tab, balloons and host helpers load with a lazily loaded Word chunk (a few KB). Opening a document that already has comments should not add a noticeable delay on typical review files.
dod: A Review tab offers New Comment, Delete, Resolve, Previous and Next; Ctrl+Alt+M adds a comment on the current selection (or the word at the caret).
The commented range is highlighted; a margin card shows author, time, the text, Reply and Resolve; Previous/Next move between comments; Delete removes the comment and its anchor as one undo step.
Saved files open in Word and LibreOffice with the comments intact (validator + round-trip in CI); a file that already has comments shows them on open.

Host API (and React equivalents): el.getComments(), el.addComment(text) using the current selection, and a nitro-comment event when a comment is added, replied to, resolved or deleted. This complements getSelection().

Playwright tests cover add, reply, resolve, delete, save round-trip and the host hooks; bundle-budget and all required checks green. No first-load size limit is raised; new code stays in the lazy Word chunk.
proposals.status_note: Declined 2026-11-20 (👎); issue closed as not planned.

proposals.headline: Headers, footers and page numbers, like Word
proposals.today_caption: Today: the Insert tab has Page Break, Tables and Picture, but no Header, Footer or Page Number, and the page's top margin is empty.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Insert > Header & Footer (Header, Footer, Page Number). The page shows a header with the document title and Page 1 of 1, as in Word.
proposals.why: Almost every professional Word document has a header, a footer or a page number, and people look for them on the Insert tab in Word, Google Docs, OnlyOffice and Collabora. Nitro already reads, paints and can set header and footer stories (the edit helpers landed with the earlier header/footer work), and the approved Print proposal will need those fields to show up on the printed page. What's missing is the Insert UI and a way to type into the header or footer in the document itself.
proposals.effort_note: 1–2 days (Insert group and in-page edit surface on top of the existing header/footer renderer and set-text helpers)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. The saved header, footer and page-number fields must be valid so Word opens the file without a repair prompt, and they must use the document's section (margins, first-page header if the file already has one). Typing in the header must not move the body text. A page-number field has to update when pages are added, not stay as a fixed '1'.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the Header & Footer group and the in-page editor load with the lazily loaded Word Insert chunk (a small addition). Headers and footers already paint on each page today when a file contains them; this does not add work on open for files without them.
dod: Insert > Header & Footer offers Header, Footer and Page Number (the Font and Paragraph groups stay at two rows; this is a new Insert group). Choosing Header or Footer (or double-clicking the top or bottom margin) edits that story in place, with a clear Header or Footer label, as in Word.

Page Number inserts a page-number field in the header or footer (user picks position: left, centre or right); the visible number updates when the page count changes, and a 3-page document shows 1, 2 and 3.

Saved files open in Word and LibreOffice with the header, footer and page numbers intact (validator + round-trip in CI); a file that already has headers or footers stays editable and is not rewritten on open.
Esc or double-clicking the body leaves header/footer edit; typography in the header uses the same font and paragraph commands as the body; undo covers the whole insert or edit as one step.
Playwright tests cover insert header, insert page number, edit, undo and a save round-trip; bundle-budget and all required checks green. No first-load size limit is raised.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-20 (👍). Queued behind the host-API priority work.

proposals.headline: Right-click menus with the everyday commands, like Office
proposals.today_caption: Today: right-clicking cell F4 does nothing; no menu appears, so Insert, Delete, Clear and Format are only on the ribbon.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Excel-style right-click menu (Cut, Copy, Paste Options, Insert…, Delete…, Clear Contents, Sort, Filter, Format Cells…) with the mini toolbar above it.
proposals.why: Right-click is how most people reach Cut, Copy, Paste, Insert row and Format Cells in Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and Google Docs, OnlyOffice and Collabora all copy it. In Nitro a right-click does nothing, so users who don't know the ribbon layout get stuck. The editor already has a context-menu framework and a Shift+F10 shortcut entry; they just aren't wired to right-click or filled with per-app commands.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (menu framework exists; per-app item lists and wiring)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. Every item must call the same command as its ribbon button, so behaviour can't drift. Right-click must first move the selection to the clicked cell, word or shape (unless it is inside the current selection), as Office does. Host apps that need the browser menu can turn it off.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the menu code and item lists load with each app's lazy ribbon chunk (a few KB). Nothing runs until the user right-clicks.
dod: Right-click (and Shift+F10 / the Menu key) opens an Office-style menu at the pointer in all three apps; Esc, click-away and arrow keys work, and it is screen-reader accessible (role=menu).
Excel: Cut, Copy, Paste Options, Insert…, Delete…, Clear Contents, Sort, Filter, Format Cells…, Row Height…, Column Width…; on row/column headers: Insert, Delete, Hide, Unhide.

Word: Cut, Copy, Paste Options, Font…, Paragraph…, Link…, bullets and numbering; PowerPoint: Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Bring to Front / Send to Back on shapes, and New Slide / Duplicate / Delete on the thumbnail rail.
Right-click moves the selection to the target first; disabled items are greyed out; a contextmenu="browser" attribute (and React prop) keeps the browser's own menu for hosts that want it.
Playwright tests cover one item per app plus keyboard open; bundle-budget and all required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-18 (👍). Queued behind the host-API priority work.

proposals.headline: Insert and edit links (Ctrl+K), with a link card on hover
proposals.today_caption: Today: the Insert tab has Page Break, Tables and Picture but no Link, and Ctrl+K does nothing (the console logs "unsupported edit op insert.link").
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Insert > Links > Link (Ctrl+K) opens an Insert link box with the selected text, an address, and links to headings in the document.
proposals.why: Adding a link to selected text is a basic editing step in Word, PowerPoint, Google Docs and every web editor. Nitro already reads and displays links in files and fires a nitro-hyperlink event when one is clicked, and Ctrl+K is already bound to an insert.link command, but the command does nothing. Finishing it lets people add, edit and remove links without leaving Nitro.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (Word first, PowerPoint text boxes next)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. The saved link needs a valid hyperlink relationship (TargetMode=External) so Word and PowerPoint open the file without repair; addresses must be checked (http/https/mailto only, no javascript:). Undo must remove the link and its relationship together.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the dialog and hover card load with the lazy Word/PowerPoint ribbon chunk (about 2–3 KB). The Rust side adds a small edit op; no effect on open time.
dod: Insert > Links > Link and Ctrl+K open an Insert link box prefilled with the selected text; Insert turns the selection into a link (blue, underlined) and is one undo step.
With the caret in a link, Ctrl+K edits it; a hover card shows the address with Copy, Edit and Remove; Ctrl+Click opens the link (fires nitro-hyperlink for hosts).
Links to headings in the same Word document work (bookmark anchors).
Saved files open in Word and PowerPoint without repair (validator + LibreOffice round-trip in CI); only http, https and mailto addresses are accepted.
Playwright tests cover insert, edit, remove and save round-trip in Word and PowerPoint; bundle-budget and all required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-18 (👍). Queued behind the host-API priority work.

proposals.headline: Print or save as PDF (Ctrl+P) with a clean print preview
proposals.today_caption: Today: the File menu has Open, Save a copy and Close but no Print. Ctrl+P in the document does nothing (console: "unsupported edit op file.print"), and the browser's own Print captures the toolbar, ribbon and status bar around the page.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: File > Print… (Ctrl+P) opens a print view with destination (Save as PDF or a printer), page range, paper size, orientation and scale, next to a clean preview of the page.
proposals.why: Printing and saving as PDF are among the most common things people do with an Office file, and Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Google Docs and OnlyOffice all have File > Print with a preview. In Nitro, Ctrl+P is already bound to a Print command that isn't implemented, so nothing happens, and printing from the browser menu includes the app's toolbar and ribbon. Rendering each page cleanly for print reuses the page painters Nitro already has.
proposals.effort_note: 3–4 days (Word and PowerPoint pages first; Excel print areas and page breaks next)
proposals.risk: Medium. Long documents must render page by page without exhausting memory (draw into the print frame lazily, cap resolution). Excel needs sensible page breaks and must honour the file's print area and fit-to-page settings. Read-only, so files can't be damaged.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the print view is its own lazily loaded chunk (a few KB). Print renders pages on demand at print resolution, so it doesn't slow normal viewing.
dod: File > Print… and Ctrl+P (inside the viewer) open a print view in all three apps; the browser's own Ctrl+P is not triggered.

The preview and output contain only the document pages (no app chrome), one per sheet of paper, using the file's paper size, margins and orientation; options for page range, scale, and in Excel selection / gridlines / fit sheet on one page.
Print sends the pages to the browser print dialog, where Save as PDF works; a host API el.print() (and React ref.print()) does the same.
Printing a 50-page docx and a 30-slide pptx completes without page errors and stays under the memory cap; Playwright test checks page count and that no chrome appears in page.pdf() output.
Bundle-budget and all required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-18 (👍). Queued behind the host-API priority work.

proposals.headline: See the word count in the status bar, with Word's Word Count box on click
proposals.today_caption: Today: the status bar only says "Page 1 of 1"; there is no way to see how long the document is.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: "105 words" sits next to the page number; clicking it opens a Word Count box (pages, words, characters, paragraphs, lines), like Word.
proposals.why: Word shows a live word count at the bottom left of every document, and anyone writing to a length limit checks it constantly. Nitro's status bar only shows the page number, so users have to paste text elsewhere to count it. A live count next to the page number, plus the familiar Word Count box on click, matches Word exactly (Google Docs has the same under Tools > Word count).
proposals.risk: Low. Read-only display; nothing is written to the file, so save and round-trip can't break.
proposals.perf: Counting runs in Rust over paragraph text after each edit, debounced to idle, so typing stays smooth on long documents. About 1 KB in the lazily loaded Word chunk plus a small WASM addition; nothing added to the first-load loader (0 B headroom).
dod: Status bar shows "N words" right after "Page X of Y" and updates within about 300 ms after typing, paste, delete and undo/redo.
With text selected it shows "S of N words", like Word.
Clicking the count opens a keyboard-accessible Word Count box (pages, words, characters with and without spaces, paragraphs, lines); Esc or Close dismisses it.
Counts match Word on notes.docx (105 words) and three corpus files; Playwright test covers count, selection and dialog; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Freeze Panes: keep header rows and label columns in view while you scroll
proposals.today_caption: Today: after scrolling, row 1 and its labels are gone, and the View tab only has Zoom and Diagnostics.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: View > Window > Freeze Panes menu (Freeze Panes, Freeze Top Row, Freeze First Column); row 1 stays pinned above the scrolled rows.
proposals.why: Freezing the top row is one of the first things people do in a real spreadsheet; without it, the column headings vanish as soon as you scroll. Nitro already reads, draws and saves frozen panes that come in a file, but users can't set or remove one, and the View tab has no Window group. A View > Freeze Panes menu matches Excel (Google Sheets has the same under View > Freeze).
proposals.effort_note: 1–2 days (drawing and saving frozen panes already exist)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. The saved sheetView pane must be valid so Excel opens the file without a repair prompt, and clicks in the frozen area must still hit the right cells.
proposals.perf: No first-load change; a few hundred bytes in the lazily loaded Excel ribbon. Scrolling uses the frozen-pane drawing path that files with panes already use.
dod: View tab gets a Window group with Freeze Panes ▾ (Freeze Panes at the selected cell, Freeze Top Row, Freeze First Column); it becomes Unfreeze Panes when a freeze is set. Home tab and the 2-row Font/Paragraph groups are untouched.
Frozen rows and columns stay in view while scrolling by mouse, keyboard and scrollbars, with the freeze line drawn; selecting cells in the frozen area works.
Undo/redo work; the saved file opens in Excel with the same freeze and no repair prompt (round-trip tests with and without an existing pane).

proposals.headline: Tell host apps when a document has unsaved changes (nitro-dirty event, el.dirty, React onDirtyChange)
proposals.today_caption: Today: a host app embeds <nitro-docx> and the user has typed, but the app has no signal and still says "Last saved 9:02 AM".
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the host header flips to "Unsaved changes" from a nitro-dirty event; the same signal drives React onDirtyChange and a before-close warning.
proposals.why: Apps that embed Nitro need to show "Unsaved changes", autosave, and warn before the tab closes, which every Office and Google editor does. Today the only unsaved-changes signal lives inside Nitro's own full ribbon; a host using the plain element or <NitroViewer> hears nothing until it calls save(), and onChange only fires on save. That tracker also works by re-saving the whole file 350 ms after each burst of typing, so an engine-side modified flag is both the missing API and a speed-up.
proposals.risk: Low. Additive API. The flag must return to clean when undo reaches the saved state, and after save() or opening a new file.
proposals.perf: Replaces the ribbon's save-and-hash check (a full save after every edit burst) with a counter from the engine's edit history: less CPU and memory churn on large files. Event wiring goes in the lazily loaded editor chunk; the first-load loader stays within budget.
dod: Editable <nitro-docx>, <nitro-xlsx> and <nitro-pptx> expose a read-only dirty property and fire nitro-dirty (detail.dirty) only when it changes; save() and loading a file reset it; undo back to the saved state makes it clean again.
React: onDirtyChange(dirty) prop and isDirty() on the ref, with TypeScript types and a README example for autosave and a before-close warning.
Nitro's own ribbon indicator uses the same signal (the save-and-hash probe is removed); the demo's leave warning still works.
Tests for all three formats (edit → dirty, undo → clean, save → clean) plus the consumer-smoke example; bundle-budget and all required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Partly shipped in v0.2.0 (tagged ee9789c, published 2026-11-22): el.dirty + nitro-change. React onDirtyChange is still in draft PR #597.

proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: a Notes pane under the slide plus a Notes toggle in the status bar, like PowerPoint.

proposals.headline: Find & Replace (Ctrl+H) in the find bar, for all three apps
proposals.today_caption: Today: the find bar finds "Q3" (1 of 2) but there's no way to replace it.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: a Replace box with Replace, Replace all, Match case and Whole word, in the same find bar.
proposals.why: Replace is one of the most-used editing commands in Word, Excel and PowerPoint. The Word engine already has Replace and Replace all inside it, but the find bar never shows them, and Excel and PowerPoint have no replace at all. This exposes it in one consistent bar with the Office shortcut, Ctrl+H.
proposals.risk: Low–medium. Replace all must be one undo step and keep formatting when a match spans styled runs; in Excel it replaces cell text only, never formula text unless asked.
proposals.perf: The find bar lives in the first-load loader, which has 0 B headroom, so the replace row must load lazily with each app's chunk. No first-load growth; a few KB per app chunk.
dod: Ctrl+H (and a Replace button next to Find) opens the find bar with a Replace row.
Replace and Replace all work in Word body and tables, Excel cell values, and PowerPoint shape text; the bar says "Replaced N".
Match case and Whole word toggles work; one Ctrl+Z undoes a whole Replace all.
Saved files validate and reopen cleanly; eager loader budget unchanged; all required checks green.
